title: Effect of an Executable Emulator Validator on Semantic Failures in LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that measured the marginal effect of inserting an executable emulator validator with a bounded repair policy into a generate→validate→repair pipeline versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) and a single shared generator call per pair (declared model: gpt-5-mini; model_calls_used = 120), identical shared candidates were scored under baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (validator±repair) conditions. The deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0) enforced structured workflow policies and permitted at most one repair iteration when violations occurred. All 120 shared candidates satisfied the emulator’s full_intent_constraint_validation rule: baseline successes = 120/120; guarded successes = 120/120; paired contingency n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. We expand methodological detail, diagnostics grounded in archived artifacts, interpretation of this ceiling outcome, and protocol recommendations to exercise validator/repair behavior in future confirmatory runs.

sections.introduction: Automating network configuration from operator intent with large language models (LLMs) promises efficiency gains but raises operational safety concerns: syntactically plausible command sequences can violate temporal, sequencing, and group-level workflow invariants that only closed-loop execution reveals. Prior executable-benchmark research argues that validation layers—emulators, digital twins, or deterministic checkers—are needed to detect and prevent semantic failures that static or token-level checks miss. This study asks a narrowly scoped, mechanistic confirmatory question under a preregistered protocol: does integrating an executable emulator validator (with a bounded repair policy) into a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce emulator-observed semantic failures relative to an LLM-only suggestion workflow for identical generator outputs? To isolate validator/repair marginal effects we used a shared-generation paired design: for each task a single generator output was produced and the identical candidate was evaluated both without (baseline) and with (guarded) the validator. This isolates the validator/repair subsystem from generator variance, enabling a clean attribution of any discordance to validation or repair mechanisms.
sections.related_work: Two complementary literature strands frame our work. First, executable, emulation‑grounded benchmarks for NetOps demonstrate that closed-loop tests find sequencing, stateful, and group-availability errors beyond syntax-level faults; recent benchmark and tool papers (e.g., NetConfArena and related executable-benchmark reports) provide empirical evidence that generate‑and‑validate workflows detect errors missed by static checks [https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23179, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22513, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18233]. Second, architectural and survey work on tool-augmented LLM agents motivates veto layers and bounded-autonomy guardrails that delegate safety‑critical checks to deterministic solvers or emulators [see architectural surveys in the verification and agentic-NetOps literature]. These works indicate both potential gains from validation and practical costs of integration. Our study complements these lines by using a shared-generation paired design to isolate the validator/repair marginal effect for identical generator outputs; this contrasts with generator-focused evaluations that conflate generator variability with verifier efficacy and highlights that experimental lensing (generator‑focused vs validator‑focused) determines what inferences are possible.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1 prior to execution. The confirmatory design was a paired binary comparison with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine; 40 tasks each). The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified primary test was the exact two‑sided McNemar; a paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified. The preregistration fixed an execution contract: paired design with shared_initial_candidate generation per task (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1), at most one repair iteration per guarded episode, deterministic harness resets, contamination checks, and explicit exclusion rules for instrumentation failures. Preregistration id: CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1.

Task corpus and structured payloads. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, natural-language intent, an explicit required_sequence, and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, level). Workflow_policies were represented as executable constraints (examples: must_be_down_for_fields, make-before-break patterns, final_group_constraints) that the emulator enforces at execution time rather than as heuristic text matches. The deterministic task manifest exercised a range of canonical policy motifs and difficulty strata (level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}). Representative task metadata (e.g., for task‑000001) show difficulty.level = "medium", required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3 in the validator trace.

Shared-generation paired protocol and instrumentation. For each task a single shared initial generation call to the declared hosted model (gpt-5-mini) produced the shared candidate; that identical candidate was then executed and scored in both baseline and guarded conditions. This decision removes generator variance across paired episodes (model_calls_used = 120; planned maximum_model_calls = 240). The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets between tasks, container checksum verification, and provider-call audits (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cache_miss_count = 120; cache_hit_count = 0). Contamination heuristics (duplicate-output detection and cross-condition cache-key reuse detection) were applied and none triggered. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed pair accounting (complete_pair_count = 120; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0).

Validator and repair semantics. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). For each shared candidate the validator executed the command sequence in the emulator from initial_state, enforced workflow_policies encoded in the task payload, and emitted a structured validator_trace recording validation_before/after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation_codes, and repair_applied. The prespecified repair policy allowed ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode when violation_count > 0; repair_provider_call artifacts would be archived if applied. In this execution validator.violation_count = 0 across all guarded episodes and validator_trace.repair_applied = false for every pair. Scoring followed the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule implemented by the validator; the binary semantic outcome (semantic_success) equaled 1 when the emulator‑observed final_state satisfied the task expected_final_state and required_sequence constraints.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary confirmatory outcome. Execution completed without technical exclusions (completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 120). Condition summaries: baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rate = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table was n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the paired difference = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; consequently no repair_provider_call artifacts were created.

Per-topology and representative diagnostics. Deterministic partitioning produced 40 tasks per topology class with perfect success in both conditions in each stratum: Edge 40/40 baseline and guarded; Core 40/40 baseline and guarded; Leaf–spine 40/40 baseline and guarded. Representative validator_trace diagnostics from archived examples illustrate the semantics: for task‑000001 parsed_command_count = 4 and required_command_count = 4; observed_touched_field_count = 3; validation_after.valid = true; repair_applied = false. For representative hard/very_hard tasks (examples in the manifest) parsed_command_count matched required_command_count and the validator recorded violation_count = 0, confirming generator outputs satisfied encoded workflow constraints across difficulty strata.

Repair incidence and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 throughout the run, no repairs occurred; secondary endpoints intended to measure repair incidence or repair-call costs are vacuous for this execution and recorded as such in the archived analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation: a ceiling outcome from a shared-generation paired design. The shared-generation paired design answers a focused mechanistic question—can a validator/repair subsystem improve outcomes for identical generator outputs?—but it necessarily leaves the validator idle when the generator produces valid candidates for the task corpus. In our execution all 120 shared candidates already satisfied the deterministic emulator validator, so the guarded pipeline could not improve on the baseline; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 and degenerate bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00] are statistical expressions of this ceiling outcome. The preregistered power calculation had assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40 and targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15; the observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions, rendering the confirmatory McNemar test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.

Design trade-offs and actionable recommendations. The paired shared-generation protocol increases internal validity for isolating validator effects but can under-exercise repair when the generator is well‑calibrated for the chosen task bank. Based on recorded difficulty metadata and the absence of repairs, practical preregistered adjustments to increase opportunities for validator/repair exercise include: (1) independent generation per condition (allow separate generator draws per condition and account for additional variance in the analysis), (2) controlled prompt perturbations (prespecify perturbation variants for a subset of tasks to raise generator error incidence), (3) task stratification toward higher-complexity strata (focus power on tasks labeled very_hard or with higher dependency_rule_count and required_command_count), and (4) exploratory arms with expanded repair budgets to observe multi-step repair dynamics. These modifications preserve the original scientific question family while enabling the guard to intercept generator-induced errors.

Operational implications and auditability. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (checked rules, parsed_command_count, touched fields, explicit repair flags) supports operator auditability, post-hoc diagnosis, and compliance reporting. Instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, deterministic reconciliation, and scorer traces) provides machine-verifiable evidence that the guarded layer was executed and whether it applied repairs—useful for operator trust and governance even in runs where the guard is idle. The experiment underscores that claims about repair benefits require careful experimental framing: if generators rarely produce invalid candidates under a frozen prompt, the guard will be idle by design.

Threats to validity. Internal validity in this run is strong: deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audits, zero exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity is limited by synthetic task payloads and validator policy encodings; the validator enforces canonical workflow invariants but does not emulate every vendor-specific behavior or partial-observability telemetry. External validity is constrained by the deterministic synthetic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Statistical conclusion validity is affected by the ceiling: the preregistered power assumptions were not met, so the primary confirmatory test cannot demonstrate the originally targeted effect size under the observed data distribution. These limitations are documented in the preregistration and archived reconciliation artifacts.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired design and the supplied synthetic task corpus (N=120, 40 per topology class), all shared initial generator outputs satisfied the deterministic emulator validator, producing identical perfect success rates for baseline and guarded conditions (n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0). The empirical result is therefore a ceiling: the guarded validator did not observe any candidate violations and applied no repairs (repair_applied = false for every guarded episode). The principal contribution is methodological and evidential: we demonstrate a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design that cleanly isolates validator/repair marginal effects for identical generator outputs, and we provide deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) that enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing. Follow-up confirmatory studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, introduce controlled prompt perturbations, concentrate on higher-complexity tasks, or expand repair budgets are required to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

Adapter/orchestration framework and validator: adapter_family = "hosted_netops_gvr_v1"; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; deterministic emulator validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). Repair policy: guarded repairs were conditional on validator-reported violations (repair_applied only when validator.violation_count>0); validator traces record repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. No contamination flags or technical exclusions occurred. Representative archival artifacts (task manifests, responses, validator traces, condition summaries, paired contingency table, and deterministic reconciliation) were archived at the time of execution for independent verification. No manual post-lock edits of technical manuscript content were performed.
limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
